release.headline: A SPECIAL DEPLOYMENT
release.description: The engineering team has finalized the custom birthday build for Kevin. All automated tests have passed. Awaiting final CTO execution.

categories.title: Added
items: New memories and milestone achievements unlocked
More wisdom points added to leadership skill tree
Another year of visionary technical leadership

categories.title: Improved
items: Problem solving velocity under complex constraints
Team building and empowering engineers to own outcomes

categories.title: Known Issues
items: Engineers still claim: "It's just a small 5-minute change."
"One quick question" continues to take at least 30 minutes.
Production incidents continue to appear at the worst possible time.
CTO remains statistically impossible to escape from in Slack threads.

steps.text: Deployment successful. Kevin v2026.09.17 is LIVE in Production!

legacy.heading: Some things don't belong in a release note.
legacy.subheading: They become part of how a team thinks.
legacy.centralTheme: You didn't just teach us how to build software. You taught us how to think about building software.

concepts.title: Domain-Driven Design
concepts.quote: You taught us to understand the domain before rushing into the code.

concepts.title: Software Architecture
concepts.quote: You taught us that good architecture is about decisions, boundaries, and the problems we're solving — not just folders and frameworks.

concepts.title: System Design
concepts.quote: You taught us to think about the system as a whole, not just the feature in front of us.

concepts.title: Engineering Thinking
concepts.quote: You pushed us to ask "Why?" before asking "How?"

concepts.title: Technical Excellence
concepts.quote: You showed us that making something work is only the beginning.

legacy.transitionText: These stopped being things you taught us.
legacy.transitionPunchline: They became the way we build.
legacy.transitionLegacy: That's probably the best part of your legacy with us.

teamMessages.heading: Every release has a team behind it.
teamMessages.subheading: Personal notes, gratitude, and birthday wishes from the engineers building alongside you.

members.name: Chandan
members.message:
Kevin,

Thank you for teaching us to look at software differently.

DDD, architecture, system design, and all the engineering principles you've shared with us have become much more than technical concepts. They have changed the way we approach problems, make decisions, and think about the systems we build.

You've pushed us to go beyond simply making things work — to understand the domain, question our decisions, think about boundaries, and care about the quality of what we create.

More importantly, you've given us the opportunity to learn, experiment, make mistakes, and grow as engineers.

Thank you for being the person who taught us not just how to build software, but how to think like engineers.

Happy Birthday, Kevin. ❤️

members.name: Satvik
members.message:
Happy Birthday Kevin! Working under your guidance has been an incredible experience. Your ability to break down complex architectural bottlenecks into actionable decisions inspires all of us every single day.

Hope you take some well-deserved time off to celebrate this milestone!

members.name: Harish
members.message:
Wishing you a fantastic Birthday, Kevin! Thank you for fostering a culture where engineering excellence meets genuine warmth and continuous learning.

Here's to building even bigger and better systems together in the coming year!

ctoStatus.heading: CTO SYSTEM STATUS
ctoStatus.subheading: Core leadership metrics, runtime diagnostics & health monitoring
ctoStatus.systemStatusNote: No critical issues detected. Although the team continues to generate unexpected requirements.

finalMessage.heading: Every engineer remembers the people who taught them to code.
finalMessage.subheading: But the people who teach us how to think stay with us much longer.
bulletPoints: You've taught us to question assumptions.
And to care about the systems we're building — not just the code we're writing.
finalMessage.closingQuote: Those lessons will travel much further than any project we've built together.
